items.item: The average chain length over all buckets equals α exactly, by simple counting, for any hash function at all, good or terrible — measuring the average alone proves nothing about a hash being well-spread. The real, hash-dependent claim is that the longest chain stays close to that average rather than hoarding keys.

items.item: Chaining's one real, named cost is a pointer per entry (the next-pointer every chain node carries) — the exact cost open addressing's in-place entry storage avoids, which is topic 18's own subject, not built here.

at.step: The one real cost: a pointer per entry

items.item: Resizing a table to keep α bounded as n grows (so the Θ(1+α) bound stays Θ(1)) is a separate mechanism, this chapter's own topic 20, not this topic's subject.

Open addressing, this chapter's very next topic, stores every entry directly in the table itself rather than in a chain, which is why it cannot simply let a bucket's chain grow past a load factor of 1.

Universal hashing's formal guarantee, which would turn the simple-uniform-hashing assumption into a provable bound rather than an assumption, is out of scope: the syllabus itself skips it for this chapter.
